question: Which world maps show every country at its true size, and which inflate some?
answer: Gall–Peters, Mollweide and Equal Earth are equal-area: each square centimetre of map covers the same ground. Mercator keeps angles instead, for navigation, and swells areas towards the poles; Robinson and Winkel tripel are compromises that bend everything a little. No flat map keeps both shapes and areas true, as Gauss's work on curved surfaces shows.
move: Every flat map gives up something; ask whether it kept area, angle or neither.
ask: Which map or chart have I trusted for something it was never designed to keep?
